title: Scaling Test-Time Compute for Mathematical and Algorithmic Reasoning
abstract: Recent frontier language models demonstrate notable capabilities, yet multi-step algorithmic and mathematical problem solving remains challenging. In this work, we investigate scaling test-time compute via guided tree search and iterative self-correction rather than solely relying on pretraining parameter scale. We introduce SearchPolicy-X, an inference framework combining Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) with a learned value model trained via Direct Preference Optimization (DPO). Evaluated across MATH, GSM8K, and OlympiadBench, our approach yields a 28.4% absolute accuracy improvement over greedy decoding on hard mathematical reasoning tasks. However, our method incurs a substantial latency overhead (4.2x inference time per token) and exhibits sensitivity to value model calibration errors in non-standard mathematical formalisms.

title: Unified Multimodal Representations via Contrastive Spatial-Temporal Alignment
abstract: Aligning vision and language representations across dynamic visual domains requires capturing both fine-grained spatial grounding and temporal continuity. We propose OmniAlign, a dual-encoder transformer architecture that introduces contrastive spatiotemporal cross-attention layers trained on paired video-text and image-caption corpora. Evaluated on MSR-VTT, ActivityNet Captions, and COCO Captions, OmniAlign achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot retrieval accuracy (82.1% Recall@1 on MSR-VTT). We identify key limitations: high GPU memory consumption during dense temporal attention prevents processing videos exceeding 90 seconds without temporal subsampling, and the model exhibits visual hallucination on dense background objects.

title: Adaptive Dense Retrieval with Dynamic Chunking for Enterprise RAG
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems frequently suffer from retrieval noise when fixed-size text chunking splits coherent conceptual boundaries. We introduce SemanticChunk-RAG, an adaptive dense retrieval framework that utilizes hierarchical semantic boundary detection combined with learned contextual reranking. Using BM25, ColBERTv2, and dense bi-encoders across MS-MARCO, NaturalQuestions, and an enterprise technical documentation benchmark, our framework improves end-to-end question answering factual accuracy by 19.3% and reduces context window token bloat by 34%. Stated limitations include indexing latency that scales quadratically with document length and degraded performance when processing low-resource domain jargon absent from the embedding vocabulary.

title: Post-Training 4-Bit Activation Quantization for Ultra-Low Latency LLM Serving
abstract: Deploying large language models with hundreds of billions of parameters requires exorbitant memory bandwidth. While weight quantization is well studied, activation quantization to 4-bit precision typically leads to catastrophic perplexity spikes due to outlier features. We present SmoothAct-4B, a hardware-aware post-training quantization method that applies channel-wise outlier smoothing and asymmetric clipping grids. We benchmark our method on LLaMA-3-70B and Mistral-Large across WikiText-2, C4, and MMLU, achieving less than 0.15 perplexity degradation while delivering a 2.6x inference speedup and 68% memory reduction on NVIDIA A100 GPUs. The primary limitation is that our custom CUDA kernels are tailored specifically to Ampere and Hopper architectures, lacking portable speedups on consumer hardware and AMD ROCm.

title: Self-Supervised Consistency Policy for Dexterous Robotic Manipulation
abstract: Learning dexterous multi-finger robotic manipulation from human video demonstrations suffers from distribution shift and expensive teleoperation data collection. We propose DexterousFlow, a self-supervised policy learning framework combining diffusion consistency models with tactile-visual sensor fusion. Using a 16-DoF allegro robotic hand evaluated on real-world manipulation tasks (in-hand pen spinning, cube reorientation, and cable threading) across 600 physical trials, DexterousFlow achieves an 84.5% task success rate with 10x faster action inference than standard diffusion policies. Stated limitations include fragility to severe lighting variations, tactile sensor calibration drift over extended operation cycles, and an inability to generalize to deformable soft objects.

title: Latent Space Temporal Flow Matching for High-Fidelity Video Synthesis
abstract: Generating long, temporally coherent video sequences with complex physics remains an open frontier in generative modeling. We introduce ChronoFlow, a continuous-time latent flow matching framework designed for high-resolution video synthesis. ChronoFlow incorporates 3D spatial-temporal rotary positional embeddings and cross-frame velocity regularization. Evaluated on UCF-101, WebVid-10M, and a curated high-definition 4K cinematic benchmark, ChronoFlow demonstrates superior FVD (Fréchet Video Distance) of 142.3 and improved motion smoothness over baseline 3D U-Nets. Limitations highlighted by the authors include high training computational expenditure (requiring over 50,000 H100 GPU hours) and occasional failure to preserve fine semantic identity in fast camera pans.

title: Geometric Equivariant Graph Transformers for Molecular Property Prediction and Drug Discovery
abstract: Accurately predicting 3D molecular properties is essential for virtual screening and computational drug discovery. Standard message-passing graph neural networks often struggle to model long-range interatomic forces and Euclidean symmetry. We present EquiChem-X, an E(3)-equivariant graph transformer that integrates learned dihedral angular encodings and continuous radial basis kernels. Evaluated on QM9, MoleculeNet, and the PDBbind database for protein-ligand binding affinity, EquiChem-X achieves top-ranking mean absolute error (MAE) on all quantum chemistry targets. Stated limitations include substantial memory overhead when scaling to large protein structures (>10,000 atoms) and reliance on static crystal structures that ignore dynamic physiological conformational ensembles.

title: Mitigating Hallucination in Long-Context LLMs via Dynamic Fact Attribution Verification
abstract: As context windows expand to millions of tokens, language models frequently hallucinate or retrieve irrelevant information when answering complex queries over lengthy transcripts. We propose FactGuard, a dynamic attribution verification framework that operates during token generation via attention-head steering and real-time citation grounding. Across LongBench, L-Eval, and synthetic Needle-In-A-Haystack benchmarks up to 128k tokens, FactGuard reduces ungrounded hallucinated claims by 41.2% while maintaining conversational fluency. However, the authors note that FactGuard adds a 18% token generation latency penalty and may produce false positive attribution warnings on figurative or conversational speech.

title: Synthetic Multi-Turn Dialogue Distillation for Task-Oriented Conversational Agents
abstract: Collecting high-quality annotated dialogue datasets for enterprise domain customer service is costly and subject to stringent privacy regulations. We introduce SynthDialog, an automated synthetic data curation pipeline that uses multi-agent debate and critique filtering to generate high-diversity conversational trajectories. Fine-tuning an 8B parameter student model on SynthDialog across MultiWOZ 2.4 and Taskmaster-1 achieves 91.2% task completion success, matching models trained on 5x larger human-annotated corpora. Limitations include vulnerability to mode collapse where generated user personas exhibit homogeneous polite phrasing, and lack of cultural dialectal variation.

title: Mechanistic Circuit Identification for Steering Safety Behaviors in Foundation Models
abstract: Understanding how safety-critical decisions are internally routed in deep transformer networks is vital for robust alignment. In this paper, we develop PathInspect, an automated circuit discovery technique using activation patching and sparse autoencoders to isolate attention heads responsible for refusal behaviors and jailbreak susceptibility. We evaluate PathInspect on Anthropic Red-Teaming, AdvGLUE, and JailbreakBench across 7B to 70B parameter models. We successfully locate localized sub-circuits responsible for refusal mechanisms and demonstrate precise feature steering without catastrophic degradation of general capabilities. Key limitations include high compute cost for exhaustive circuit search across all layers and heuristic thresholds in defining circuit boundary criteria.

title: Hierarchical Multi-Agent Orchestration for Autonomous Software Engineering
abstract: Recent autonomous coding agents demonstrate capability on self-contained scripts but fail on large, multi-repository software engineering benchmarks requiring iterative debugging and architectural refactoring. We present CodeOrchestrator, a hierarchical multi-agent framework comprising a tech lead planner, file system inspector, code synthesis worker, and continuous integration testing agent. Evaluated on SWE-bench Verified and HumanEval-X, CodeOrchestrator resolves 36.4% of real-world GitHub issues. Stated limitations include vulnerability to infinite execution loops during test failures, significant cumulative token cost ($3.80 per resolved issue), and difficulty navigating complex legacy build configurations.

title: Transferable Adversarial Attacks and Jailbreak Defense for Vision-Language Models
abstract: While safety alignment has progressed for text-only language models, multimodal models remain acutely vulnerable to typography-based and adversarial visual perturbations that circumvent system safety guardrails. We propose ShieldVLM, a dual defense framework that combines visual perturbation smoothing with latent safety vector projection. Evaluated against typography attacks, visual jailbreak benchmarks (MM-SafetyBench), and transfer attacks on GPT-4V and LLaVA-1.5, ShieldVLM improves benign prompt retention to 98.7% while neutralizing 89.4% of visual jailbreak prompts. Limitations include slight drop in fine-grained OCR accuracy on dense textual images and computational overhead during input smoothing preprocessing.
